breakdown.headline: Spurs 2–0 Crystal Palace

verdict.text: The result matched the chances: 3.47 xG to 0.14.

moments.text: Goal: Van Hecke from a corner (xG 0.43)

style.label: Field tilt (share of passes in opposition half)

howSpursPlayed: Spurs had 79.0% of the ball and 92.2% of the passing in the opposition half, against a season average of 62.9%.
They took 34 shots (9 on target) worth 3.47 xG, about 0.10 per shot; Crystal Palace had 2 shots worth 0.14 xG.
The match changed after half-time: Spurs' xG difference went from +0.70 in the first half to +2.45 in the second.
Momentum: Spurs on top, 11–36'; Spurs on top, 38–90.5'.
In short: dominated the ball, pinned the opponent back, short, patient passing, relied on set pieces, took players on.

setup.formationNote: Formation and positions as listed on ESPN's team sheet: the nominal shape, not a measured one.

summary: Spurs lined up in a 4-2-3-1 against Crystal Palace's 3-4-2-1 (1 change from the Chelsea game).
The result matched the chances: 3.47 xG to 0.14.
Compared with their other league games, Spurs got into the box more (67 vs 29), had more of the ball (79% vs 61%), played higher up the pitch (92% vs 68%), conceded less (0.14 xG vs 1.23 xG).
Van Hecke was the biggest attacking threat (1.12 xG + xA); Tonali won the ball back most often (6 tackles won + interceptions).

phases.title: Build-up and possession

rows.label: Long balls, share of accurate passes

read: Spurs had 79% of the ball (season average 61%), completing 759 of 815 passes (93%).
92% of all passing in the opposition half was by Spurs (field tilt), well above their usual 68%. They spent long spells camped in Crystal Palace's half.
17% of Spurs' accurate passes were in their own half (131 own half, 628 opposition half): most of the passing happened high up the pitch.
Long balls made up 1.2% of accurate passes (well below the season's 3.6%), with 60% of long balls finding a teammate. Spurs built short and rarely went direct.

phases.title: Chance creation
read: 34 shots (9 on target) worth 3.47 xG, 0.10 per shot; the season average is 0.07 per shot, so the chances were better quality than usual.
24 shots came from inside the box and 10 from outside (29% from distance).
Spurs created 6 big chances and missed 4 (season average 2.0).
67 touches in Crystal Palace's box, well above the season average of 29; Crystal Palace had 2 in Spurs' box.
Where the xG came from: open play 1.72 (52%), fast breaks 0.08, set pieces 1.50. 18 of the shots came straight from a teammate's pass (assisted).

phases.title: Finishing
read: Spurs scored 2 from 3.47 xG: 1.5 fewer than the chances were worth.
Shots on target were worth 3.11 xGOT against 3.47 xG before the shot: too many shots were off target or easy for the keeper.

phases.title: Out of possession
read: PPDA (estimated): 3.0 Crystal Palace passes in their own half per Spurs defensive action; season average 4.3. Lower means a more aggressive press, so this was a more intense press than usual.
16 tackles won and 9 interceptions (season averages 18.0 and 7.8); 7 clearances and 1 blocks.
Duels: Spurs won 57, Crystal Palace 56 (50% for Spurs); 62% of aerial duels won.
Crystal Palace managed 2 shots worth 0.14 xG (Spurs usually concede 1.23 xG) and 0 big chances.

phases.title: Transitions and set pieces
read: Fast breaks: Spurs had 1 shot on the break (0.08 xG); Crystal Palace had 0 (0.00 xG), against a season average of 1.4 shots conceded on the break.
Set pieces: 11 Spurs shots (1.50 xG, 2 goals); Crystal Palace 1 (0.11 xG, 0 goals). Corners: 19–0.

flow: First half: 0.74 xG for, 0.04 against (1–0). Second half: 2.56 for, 0.11 against (1–0). The balance shifted towards Spurs after half-time.
Spells on top (momentum index): Spurs 11–36'; Spurs 38–90.5'.
25' Spurs goal: Gray from a corner (xG 0.18).
73' Spurs goal: Van Hecke from a corner (xG 0.43).
Crystal Palace played with ten men after Mateta's red card (13'); figures after that point reflect the numbers difference.
